messages:
riley-infra: FYI rolling KMS policy change in eu-west-2 looks like it's preventing a subset of GPU nodes from decrypting node keys during join. seeing a bunch of "AccessDenied" in the keystore logs.

sam-sre: showing same in staging?

riley-infra: staging is clean, only prod eu-west-2 warm-pool and on-demand joins failing. small fraction (~6%) of new nodes.

jules-security: recent policy added an 'aws:PrincipalOrgID' condition for tighter tenant separation. probably too strict for the ephemeral service account used by our provisioner.

anna-platform: can we fallback to us-west-2 for new capacity while we fix this? cost will be higher but keeps SLA.

riley-infra: short-term fallback is possible but we have regional capacity caps. routing also touches data residency for some customers. need approval from security/compliance for cross-region fallback.

jules-security: compliance ok for non-sensitive workloads, but we need an audit trail and explicit allowlist entry for the provisioner role. prefer we land a minimal policy tweak instead of broad allowlists.

riley-infra: minimal tweak proposal: allow decrypt for principal arn:aws:sts::*:assumed-role/gpu-provisioner/* when request originates from eu-west-2 VPC endpoints (condition on aws:SourceIp or aws:SourceVpc).

sam-sre: can we patch the provisioner to use a different role that already exists in the KMS allowlist? fast path would be role-swap and redeploy.

anna-platform: role-swap looks fastest. note: deploy-bot will block if the keystore check fails preflight.

deploy-bot: deploy aborted — preflight keystore-check failed for service/gpu-provisioner in eu-west-2 :warning:

riley-infra: attaching sample log for context:
```
2026-03-22T09:14:12Z keystore-proxy error decrypt failed: AccessDenied on Key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01 - principal arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/gpu-provisioner/i-0abc1234
```

jules-security: quick mitigation options ranked: 1) temporary role-swap + allowlist entry 2) add SourceVpc condition to KMS policy to include provisioner VPC 3) rollback orgID condition (bad). prefer 1 or 2.

sam-sre: risk with 2 is we have multiple provisioner VPCs (prod, warmpool, canary). need a single condition that covers all without opening to entire region. aws:SourceVpc supports list. we can enumerate warmpool VPC and prod VPC IDs.

anna-platform: operations note — if we take role-swap, warm-pool nodes will still need to re-run join flow. expect ~10–15m of reduced warm capacity. cost impact: small increase in on-demand starts for the fallback region (~$3k/day estimate if sustained).

riley-infra: I'm going to try role-swap on a single canary AZ (eu-west-2a). will coordinate with oncall.

jules-security: please capture an audit log event with the key-id and principal and tag the ticket. I'll fast-track the allowlist change once we confirm it's the principal mismatch.

sam-sre: if canary succeeds, we push a temp policy change that adds the provisioner principal with SourceVpc condition and set a 24h automatic revert. also add a monitoring alert for increased decrypt errors.

anna-platform: adding runbook refs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-decrypt-failure and https://redwood.internal/playbooks/region-fallbacks

riley-infra: canary started — switch role to role:gpu-provisioner-alt on one provisioner pod. pinging once join completes.

riley-infra: canary node joined cleanly. join time ~38s. no errors in keystore-proxy.

jules-security: I created request ID RF-4527, added the provisioner principal to a scoped allowlist with SourceVpc condition (vpc-0aa1bb2c, vpc-0cc3dd4e). change scheduled and applied. audit log retained.

sam-sre: rolling warm-pool joins now completing. monitoring alert cleared after 4 nodes.

anna-platform: filing a postmortem item: tighten policy rollout checklist — include a preflight validation that includes ephemeral roles and warmpool principals.

riley-infra: agreed. will add a step to keystore policy playbook to run a simulated decrypt against all provisioner identities before enforcement.

jules-security: thanks — will coordinate a follow-up to codify source VPC allowlist automation. :thumbsup:

anna-platform: closing loop with customers impacted by region cap; ops note posted to #customer-success.

riley-infra: thanks team. leaving the temporary policy in place for 24h, then we'll revert to orgID-only once we finish role-tagging.

sam-sre: leaving a TODO — add metric for 'keystore.decrypt.denied' to billing dashboard so we can correlate cost impact if warmpool fails again.

jules-security: and tag related change RFC for next security review cycle.
